Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Washington. September 4th, 1917. The Superintendent. Fort Lapwai Indian School. Lapwai, Idaho. My dear Mr. Breid: The application of Mrs. Jennie Edwards for the enrollment of her son, Harry Edwards, is hereby approved. Transportation will be forwarded at an early date. Very respectfully, Superintendent. Harry Edwards See Dr. Breud's letter Oct. 14, 1918 in "Enrollment of pupils" folder Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. Oct. 8, 1918. Dr. Chas. A. Buchanan, Tulalip, Washington. Dear Doctor: We are entirely out of application forms 5-192 a, and would thank you for a loan of as many as you can possibly spare us. Thanking you in anticipation of the favor, I am, Yours very respectfully, Superintendent Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. Oct. 8, 1918. Dr. Jacob Reid, Supt. Ft. Lapwai Indian School, Lapwai, Idaho. Dear Doctor: Please remit to this office $6.75 of funds belonging to Harry Edwards at your earliest convenience, this amount being needed to settle the expense of his return to the Cushman School in September 1918. The money sent Harry by his mother was all given to him when he returned home for the vacation, none being kept on deposit in this office for his return fare, hence the necessity of the remittance requested. Thanking you in anticipation of the favor, I am, Yours very respectfully, Superintendent DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE CUSHMAN INDIAN TRADES SCHOOL, Tacoma, Wash., Aug. 18, 1917. Hon. Cato Sells, Comr. Indian Affairs, My Dear Mr. Sells: I have the honor to inclose herewith a letter from Doctor Jacob Bried, Superintendent Fort Lapwai school, transmitting an application for the enrollment of Harry Edwards who has but [blacked out] Indian Blood, but whose mother is an enrolled member of the Nez Perce Tribe. It appears that this boy is not in reach of any school and has never attended school and cannot school from his home. I think this boy should have an opportunity to attend school and would request that the necessary authority be granted for his enrollment. Please return the Superintendents letter and the application with instructions as to what action should be taken on the matter. Very respectfully, Superintendent 5-1142 DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE FORT LAPWAI INDIAN SCHOOL LAPWAI, IDAHO June 6, 1919. Mr. E. A. Hammond, Supt., Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. My dear Mr. Hammond: We have a request from the parents of Harry Edwards, a pupil in your school, that he be permitted to come home for summer vacation. His parents are willing to put up the necessary funds for transportation. This boy was not included among those for whom you sent vacation requests for signature of parents. Very respectfully, Jacob B. Reid Superintendent. Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., June 9, 1919 Dr. Jacob Breid, Supt. Lapwai, Idaho Dear Sir: Enclosed herewith find Vacation request for Harry Edwards. Kindly have this request signed and return it to this office as soon as possible. Very respectfully, Superintendent. /MG Enc. Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., June 23, 1919 Jane Edwards c/o Dr. Jacob Breid, Supt. Lapwai, Idaho Dear Madam: Enclosed herewith find Official Receipt No. 176028, covering deposit of $14.00 for Harry Edwards. Very respectfully, Superintendent. /MG Enc. VACATION REQUEST FOR PUPIL. We, the undersigned, respectfully request that leave of absence be granted Harry Edwards from June 15, 1919 to September 5, 1919 to enable him to visit his home. We hereby agree to pay all expenses, including round-trip railroad fares, sleeping-car fares, meals, lodging, stage fares, telegraph and telephone messages, and other incidental expenses connected with the visit. We further agree that said pupil shall be returned to the Cushman Indian school on or before the last day of the leave of absence. We further agree to deposit with the superintendent of the school sufficient money to defray all expenses to be incurred, and should the pupils, or any one of them, fail to return to school at such time as may be agreed upon by the parents or guardian and the superintendent of the school in which the pupils are enrolled, the amount of money remaining with the superintendent, necessary to the return transportation of the pupil or pupils so neglecting to return, shall be forfeited to the Government; provided, however, that in all cases where it can be shown that there were justifiable reasons for the failure of the return of the pupil the forfeiture of the funds shall not take place. If the pupil neglecting to return is from a reservation, the superintendent of the reservation shall certify to the reasons for the nonreturn of the pupil or pupils. If a pupil's home is not on a reservation, then the certificate of some reputable, disinterested citizen of the community may be requested as to the reasons for the nonreturn of the pupil or pupils. Father. Janie Edwards Mother. Guardian. Date: NOTE TO DISBURSING OFFICERS.—All receipts under this agreement must be accounted for officially as Individual Indian Money. However, any forfeitures must be transferred to Miscellaneous Receipts, Class I, and deposited in the Treasury to the credit of the United States. DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE FORT LAPWAI INDIAN SCHOOL LAPWAI, IDAHO June 19, 1919. Mr. E. H. Hammond, Supt., Gushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. My dear Mr. Hammond: Enclosed herewith find vacation request signed by Jane Edwards, mother of Harry Edwards, also her check to your order for $14 to cover round trip expenses of her son. Very respectfully, [signature] Jacob Bredt Superintendent. 5-1142 DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Fort Lapwai Indian School, Lapwai, Idaho. Aug. 8, 1917. Mr. T. B. Wilson, Supt., Cushman Trades School, Tacoma, Wash. Dear Sir: I am enclosing herewith application for the enrollment of Harry Edwards in your institution for a period of five years. This boy is but seven years of age, and has never been in school, but speaks English well. He is practically a white boy, being but [blacked-out] Indian blood, but his mother is an enrolled Nez Perce Indian. The parents live on a cattle ranch along the breaks of the Salmon River and are about eight miles from a public school. It is impossible for them, so the mother tells me, to educate the boy, and they are very anxious to place him in an Indian school. If you will admit him you may return the application, and two copies will be prepared and forwarded to you. An early reply will be much appreciated. Very respectfully, Jacob Breid, Superintendent. DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE FORT LAPWAI INDIAN SCHOOL LAPWAI, IDAHO September 1, 1919. Mr. E. H. Hammond, Supt., Tacoma, Wn. Dear Mr. Hammond: Please place transportation to my order for Harry Edwards, the pupil excused for vacation. He is ready to go and will start as soon as I receive transportation for him. Very truly, [signature] Superintendent. Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., Sept. 3, 1919 Dr. Jacob Breid, Supt. Ft. Lapwai Indian School Lapwai, Idaho. Dear Doctor: In compliance with your request of September 1st, I enclose my check, No. 728, for $7.00 in favor of Harry Edwards to pay his transportation to Cushman. This closes out his balance on my books and represents one-half the amount sent to pay his transportation home and return to Cushman. Very truly yours, Superintendent. OHK:MG Etc. CASE RECORD. This form must be executed in duplicate when a child is transferred from a reservation to a nonreservation school. The Superintendent of the nonreservation school will retain the original for his files, and the duplicate shall be deposited in the reservation school records. The reservation superintendent should send to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate as provided by law. All the blank spaces for any part of the blank is not known, that fact should be stated. No space should be left unblacked. If neither the parents are living or dead, their names must be given. The person who signs the blank as consenting to the transfer should indicate his relation to the applicant by marking out the word "parent," "guardian," or "next of kin," leaving unmarked only the title appropriate to the signer. INDORSEMENTS. The laws relating to the transfer of Indian children from reservations and schools are as follows: That hereafter no Indian child shall be sent from any Indian reservation to a school beyond the State or Territory in which said reservation is situated without the voluntary consent of the father or mother of such child if either of them are living, and if neither of them are living without the voluntary consent of the next of kin of such child. Such consent shall be made before the agent of the reservation, and he shall send to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate that such consent has been voluntarily given before such child shall be removed from such reservation. And it shall be unlawful for any Indian agent or other employee of the Government to induce, or seek to induce, by withholding rations or by other improper means, the parents or next of kin of any Indian to consent to the removal of any Indian child beyond the limits of any reservation. (28 Stats., p. 906.) Provided, That hereafter no Indian child shall be taken from any school in any State or Territory to a school in any other State against its will or without the written consent of its parents. (29 Stats., p. 348.) That no Indian pupil under the age of fourteen years shall be transported at Government expense to any Indian school beyond the limits of the State or Territory in which the parents of such child reside or of the adjoining State or Territory. (35 Stat. L., 781.) The rules provide that— A pupil who has been regularly enrolled in a nonreservation school must not be taken to any other nonreservation school without the consent of both superintendents and the Commissioner of Indian Affairs, and superintendents will be held to strict accountability for such pupils taken to their schools. An Indian boy or girl 18 years old and over may, without the consent of parents or others, personally sign the application form on its being changed to suit the case; but in all cases where the parents are living they should first be consulted. This form is to be used only in transfers from reservations or Indian schools to nonreservation schools.
